inicio.kicker: LOOP-R Engineering Track · course 4 of 6 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: Autonomous Loop Security: an agent that runs on its own can't have everything at once
inicio.lead: Lethal trifecta, Rule of Two, injection through the content it reads, per-step permissions, guard hooks, a proven sandbox, a gate for the irreversible, and an audit of your loop. Defense for people who run their own agents, with local rehearsals that don't use your quota.
inicio.capa_alt: Dark server room with a rack behind a glass door locked with a small padlock.
inicio.aulas_sub: In the order you close the doors: map the risk, limit what each session combines, see the injection, permissions, hooks, sandbox, the irreversible, and the audit.

itens: People who run Claude Code or Codex on their own for hours, in a loop, cron or systemd, on their own projects.
People who gave the agent access to read issues, pages or emails and access to the repository at the same time.
People who want to know, with proof, what the agent can and can't do on their own machine.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Map each loop session onto the three legs of the trifecta and the Rule of Two, and cut where it closes.
Separate whoever reads outside content from whoever holds the secret, and catch a leak with a canary.
Write deny rules per step, turn on hooks that deny the irreversible, and prove the sandbox holds.
Put sending, push and deleting behind a human gate and audit the loop with a dated checklist.
Linux with git, Python 3 and Node. macOS works for almost everything; the sandbox and systemd proofs are Linux-only.
Claude Code and Codex signed in through your subscription, only for the steps marked "real".
Recommended: course 0 (Foundations). Course 2 (Long Runs) runs the loop that this course protects.
